node.title: L1 decorated shift-pair gcd descent and sharpness
node.statement: For a decorated record AQ1-BQ2=R, let D=gcd(Q1,Q2) have degree c. Dividing by D gives a primitive record with reduced cofactor degree e-c and increased effective cancellation depth w+c; primitive uniqueness applies whenever e<=w+2c. The common gcd divides R, is coprime to ABN, and all its domain roots lie in the common agreement core G. An explicit F_13 family at w=1,e=2 gives ten primitive cross-coprime decorations of one ordered split pair, each realized by an exact shell pair for a corresponding received word. Thus after gcd descent the e'>w' branch must retain its received-word/Toeplitz owner; the family is not a fixed-word multiplicity or an L1 counterexample.
